rationale: 2 Peter 2:4-5 places 'the angels when they sinned... cast... into hell, placing them in chains of darkness to be held for judgment' and 'the ancient world... the flood... Noah' in one sentence-pair (BSB), and 6:8's 'Noah... found favor in the eyes of the LORD' directly anticipates 2:5's 'preserved Noah.' The Noah half of this pairing is tight and largely undisputed; the angels half depends on reading 'sons of God' in 6:2 and 6:4 as angelic beings, one of three named positions this lesson reports rather than this passage's own stated identification. Graded allusion, not quotation, because 2 Peter cites no formula and names no chapter; graded strong, not explicit, because the angelic identification itself remains a disputed reading rather than a plain restatement of Genesis 6's own wording.
